statements.impact_statement: CVE-2019-1010023 is a report against the dynamic loader of the GNU C Library (glibc) that running ldd on a crafted ELF file whose segments overlap the loader can execute code from it (https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=22851, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2019-1010023). This owner does not contain glibc. Unpacked every published activemq-artemis package, from 2.55.0-0 to the current 2.57.0-7, for amd64 and arm64 (2.57.0-0 was published for arm64 only) in the DHI Debian repository, including the files inside the jar archives it bundles. It is a Java application. Its Linux native code is six shared library files: libartemis-native-64.so and libartemis-native-32.so, each shipped both on disk and inside a jar, and Netty's epoll transport libraries for x86-64 and aarch64; every one of them lists the system libc.so.6 in NEEDED. Each package also carries, inside its jars, artemis-service.exe, a .NET Windows service wrapper, and Netty's macOS (Mach-O) kqueue library (libnetty_transport_native_kqueue_x86_64.jnilib); neither is glibc. None of them contains a static archive or a copy of libc.so.6, the dynamic loader or libc.a. glibc reaches an image only through the separate libc6 package, which is not part of this owner.

CVE-2019-1010023 is a report against the dynamic loader of the GNU C Library (glibc) that running ldd on a crafted ELF file whose segments overlap the loader can execute code from it; the glibc maintainers do not treat it as a security vulnerability, because ldd is not meant to be run on untrusted binaries. https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=22851 and https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2019-1010023. This package does not contain glibc. Checked the contents of all 100 published airflow packages in the DHI Debian repository, 3.3.0-0 to 3.4.0-9 for amd64 and arm64 (no debug-symbol packages are published for this source), recursing into the wheel and jar files they bundle; every download was checked against the checksum in the package index. Builds 3.3.0-0 to 3.4.0-0 hold 27 ELF files each, all Python extension modules dynamically linked against the system libc.so.6, and no other native code. Builds 3.4.0-1 to 3.4.0-9 add NumPy, SciPy and Ray and hold 405 to 424 ELF files each. All but 15 of them list libc.so.6 as a dependency, among them the py-spy, Ray raylet and Ray gcs_server programs. Of those 15, seven are NumPy and SciPy extension modules with no libc.so.6 entry of their own, which use the C library already loaded by the Python interpreter, and eight are the JNA dispatch libraries for FreeBSD, OpenBSD and Solaris inside Ray's ray_dist.jar, which are built for those systems and not for Linux. Those builds also carry NumPy's static archives libnpymath.a and libnpyrandom.a, whose nine members are NumPy's own math and random-distribution objects; 31 native Windows PE files with no .NET CLR header (the launcher .exe files of distlib, of setuptools and of the pip and setuptools wheels that virtualenv embeds, and JNA's three Windows jnidispatch.dll files); and JNA's two macOS (Mach-O) jnidispatch libraries. No ELF file in any build is statically linked. No file in any build is a copy of libc.so.6, the dynamic loader, libc.a or another glibc library, and none carries the glibc version banner. Ray's ray_dist.jar in builds 3.4.0-1 to 3.4.0-9 also holds JNA's two AIX dispatch libraries (libjnidispatch.a for aix-ppc and aix-ppc64), which despite the .a name are XCOFF shared objects built for AIX, not static archives, and are not glibc. The C library airflow runs against comes from glibc's own packages, such as libc6.

CVE-2019-1010023 is a report against the dynamic loader of the GNU C Library (glibc) that running ldd on a crafted ELF file whose segments overlap the loader can execute code from it; the glibc maintainers do not treat it as a security vulnerability, because ldd is not meant to be run on untrusted binaries. https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=22851 and https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2019-1010023. This package does not contain glibc. Listed the contents and read the ELF headers of every published alloy-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository: 1.18.1-0 to 1.22.0-16, 43 versions on amd64 and 44 on arm64 (1.21.2-0 is published for arm64 only), 87 packages, each matched to the repository's SHA-256 checksum; no debug-symbol packages are published for this source. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/alloy. /usr/bin/alloy is the only ELF file in every package: a Go program built with cgo, whose dynamic section names only libc.so.6 and the dynamic loader (ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 in all 43 amd64 builds, ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 in all 44 arm64 builds), so it uses the system C library at run time. No package contains libc.so.6, a dynamic loader, libc.a or another static archive, a gconv module, or a PE or Mach-O file. A search of /usr/bin/alloy in 1.18.1-0 and 1.22.0-16 (amd64) and 1.21.2-1 (arm64) found no glibc version banner, while the same search finds the libc.so.6 name in each. The C library alloy runs against comes from glibc's own packages, such as libc6.

CVE-2019-1010023 is a report against the dynamic loader of the GNU C Library (glibc) that running ldd on a crafted ELF file whose segments overlap the loader can execute code from it (https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=22851, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2019-1010023). This package does not contain glibc. Unpacked all 78 azure-functions-python packages published in the DHI Debian repository, 4.1053.100-1 to 4.1056.200-3 (including the current files of 4.1056.200-2 and 4.1056.200-3, each of which was republished under the same version), which are published for amd64 only (no arm64 build and no debug-symbol packages are published for this source), including the Azure Functions extension bundle each one carries; none of them contains a zip, wheel, jar or NuGet archive. None of them contains libc.so.6, the dynamic loader, a static C library, a gconv converter module or the glibc version banner, and none ships a static archive (.a). The package is the .NET-based Azure Functions host with its Python language workers. Each package has 45 to 48 ELF files (the .NET runtime and its host programs, the Python workers' extension modules, and the extension bundle's Linux native libraries, including librdkafka and libmsalruntime); none of them is statically linked, and every one lists the system libc.so.6 as a dynamic dependency except the two copies of alpine-librdkafka.so in the extension bundle, which are built for Alpine Linux and link musl's libc.musl-x86_64.so.1 instead. Most of its other binary content is managed .NET assemblies (845 to 854 PE files with a CLR header per package, which the bundled .NET runtime loads); the extension bundle also carries 38 native Windows libraries (PE files without a CLR header, such as the Windows builds of librdkafka, libcurl, OpenSSL and the Visual C++ runtime) and four native macOS libraries (Mach-O builds of librdkafka and the MSAL runtime), none of which is glibc. glibc reaches an image only through the separate libc6 package, built from the glibc source, which is not part of this owner and is assessed on its own.

CVE-2019-1010023 is a report against the dynamic loader of the GNU C Library (glibc) that running ldd on a crafted ELF file whose segments overlap the loader can execute code from it; the glibc maintainers do not treat it as a security vulnerability, because ldd is not meant to be run on untrusted binaries, and Debian rates it unimportant. https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=22851 and https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2019-1010023. This owner does not contain glibc. Unpacked all 51 binary packages published from the curl source in the DHI Debian repository, each checked against the index SHA256: three builds of curl 8.14.1, one made from Debian's 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 source and two from its 8.14.1-2+deb13u7 source, for amd64 and arm64, namely curl, libcurl4t64, libcurl3t64-gnutls, libcurl4-openssl-dev, libcurl4-gnutls-dev and libcurl4-doc, and the debug-symbol packages curl-dbgsym, libcurl4t64-dbgsym and libcurl3t64-gnutls-dbgsym. Apart from the detached debug-information files in the debug-symbol packages, each build ships three ELF files per architecture, none statically linked: the curl program, which uses the system dynamic loader (/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 on amd64, /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 on arm64), and the libcurl.so.4.8.0 (OpenSSL) and libcurl-gnutls.so.4.8.0 (GnuTLS) shared libraries; all three list libc.so.6 as a dependency. The debug-symbol packages hold only detached debug information for those three files, with no executable code. The development packages also ship the static archives libcurl.a and libcurl-gnutls.a, each with 179 members, all of them libcurl's own object files. No package contains a PE or Mach-O file. None of the packages contains libc.so.6, the dynamic loader, libc.a, a glibc gconv module or any other copy of glibc, and no archive member is a C library object; the same scan finds libc.so.6, the dynamic loader and the glibc version banner in the libc6 package. glibc is provided by glibc's own packages, such as libc6, and is assessed there.

The reported attack runs ldd on a crafted ELF, as one example of loading untrusted code. glibc says ldd is not expected to be used with untrusted executables (SECURITY.md, Crafted binaries and ldd), since loading a binary already gives it the caller's privileges, and DHI accepts that boundary. https://sourceware.org/pipermail/glibc-bugs/2018-February/041176.html

CVE-2019-1010023 is a report against the dynamic loader of the GNU C Library (glibc) that running ldd on a crafted ELF file whose segments overlap the loader can execute code from it; the glibc maintainers do not treat it as a security vulnerability, because ldd is not meant to be run on untrusted binaries. https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=22851 and https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2019-1010023. This package does not contain glibc. Unpacked all 44 published k8s-sidecar packages in the DHI Debian repository, 2.10.1-0 to 2.14.3-7 for amd64 and arm64, each checked against the checksum in the package index, recursing into the archive files they bundle; no debug-symbol packages are published for this source. Each holds the k8s-sidecar Python application in a virtual environment under /usr/lib/k8s-sidecar, whose python links point to the system /usr/bin/python3.14, so it ships no Python interpreter binary of its own. Its ELF files are Python extension modules: 5 per package up to 2.13.3-0, 13 in 2.14.1-0 and 14 from 2.14.1-1. All of them are shared objects that list libc.so.6 as a dependency; none lacks it and none is statically linked. The packages up to 2.14.1-0 also carry pip, whose vendored distlib holds six native Windows launcher executables (t32.exe, t64.exe, t64-arm.exe, w32.exe, w64.exe and w64-arm.exe, none with a .NET CLR header), and python-dateutil's dateutil-zoneinfo.tar.gz, which holds time-zone data files and a METADATA file and no native code; later packages include neither. No package contains a static archive, a Mach-O file, a zip, wheel or jar archive, or a file named like libc.so.6, the dynamic loader, libc.a or a gconv module, and none carries the glibc version banner; the only file in any package that names the GNU C Library is python-dateutil's tz.py, in a documentation reference to the C library's TZ variable. The C library k8s-sidecar runs against comes from glibc's own packages, such as libc6.

CVE-2019-1010023 is in the dynamic loader of the GNU C Library (glibc), which ldd uses and which can be made to map a crafted ELF file over itself, https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=22851: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2019-1010023. This package does not contain glibc. Checked the contents of every package published as memcached in the DHI Debian repository, for amd64 and arm64: the memcached 1.6.45 builds hold one binary, /usr/bin/memcached, dynamically linked against the system libc.so.6, and the earlier memcached 0.16.0 and 0.17.0 builds, like the memcached-dev 0.16.0 and 0.17.0 packages built from the same source, hold one binary, /usr/bin/memcached_exporter, a statically linked Go program built with cgo disabled (CGO_ENABLED=0) that contains no C library at all. None of them contains a copy of libc.so.6, the dynamic loader or libc.a. glibc reaches an image only through the separate libc6 package, which is not part of this owner.

CVE-2019-1010023 is in the dynamic loader of the GNU C Library (glibc): running ldd on a crafted pair of ELF files can execute code, which upstream does not treat as a security issue. https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=22851, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2019-1010023. This package does not contain glibc or ldd. Unpacked every binary package published from the ncurses source in the DHI Debian repository for amd64 and arm64 (56 index entries in 50 distinct files, because the architecture-independent ncurses-base, ncurses-term and ncurses-doc are listed for both): both published rebuilds of Debian's ncurses 6.5+20250216-2 (libtinfo6, libncurses6, libncursesw6, libncurses-dev, ncurses-bin, ncurses-base, ncurses-term, ncurses-doc and ncurses-examples, and the debug-symbol packages for libtinfo6, libncurses6, libncursesw6, ncurses-bin and ncurses-examples). None of them contains libc.so.6, the dynamic loader, libc.a, libpthread or another glibc library, the glibc version banner, a statically linked program, a PE or Mach-O file, or a jar, whl, zip or nupkg archive. The shared libraries (libtinfo, libtic, libncurses, libncursesw, libform, libformw, libmenu, libmenuw, libpanel and libpanelw) and the programs in ncurses-bin (clear, infocmp, tabs, tic, toe, tput and tset) and ncurses-examples are dynamically linked ELF files that list the system libc.so.6 in NEEDED, and the programs name the system dynamic loader (ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 or ld-linux-aarch64.so.1) as their interpreter. libncurses-dev ships twelve static archives (libncurses.a, libncursesw.a, libtinfo.a, libtic.a, libform.a, libformw.a, libmenu.a, libmenuw.a, libpanel.a, libpanelw.a, libncurses++.a and libncurses++w.a, plus libcurses.a and libtermcap.a as symlinks to two of them) whose members are ncurses's own object files; a program that links them statically takes its C library from its own build, not from this package. The debug-symbol packages hold detached debug information, and ncurses-base, ncurses-term and ncurses-doc hold terminfo entries, tab-set files and documentation with no ELF files or archives. glibc reaches an image through the separate libc6 package, which is not part of this owner and is assessed on its own.

CVE-2019-1010023 is a report against the dynamic loader of the GNU C Library (glibc) that running ldd on a crafted ELF file whose segments overlap the loader can execute code from it; the glibc maintainers do not treat it as a security vulnerability, because ldd is not meant to be run on untrusted binaries, and Debian rates it unimportant. https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=22851 and https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2019-1010023. This package does not contain glibc. Unpacked every postgresql-15 package published in the DHI Debian repository, 15.19-1 (PostgreSQL 15.19) and 15.2-0 (PostgreSQL 15.20, as the server's version string shows; it sorts below 15.19-1), on amd64 and arm64, each checked against the checksum in the package index; no debug-symbol packages are published for it. Each package holds 122 ELF programs and shared objects, none statically linked. The 37 programs use the system dynamic loader (/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 on amd64, /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 on arm64) and list libc.so.6 as a dependency. 39 server modules on amd64 and 38 on arm64 list no libc.so.6 of their own (37 and 36 have no dependencies at all, earthdistance.so needs only libm.so.6 and sslinfo.so only libcrypto.so.3) and take C library symbols from the postgres process that loads them. The nine static archives (libpq.a, libecpg.a, libecpg_compat.a, libpgtypes.a, libpgport.a, libpgport_shlib.a, libpgcommon.a, libpgcommon_shlib.a and libpgfeutils.a, 180 members) hold PostgreSQL's own object files and no C library object. Each package also ships 939 (15.19-1) or 940 (15.2-0) LLVM bitcode files used for JIT compilation, which are not native code. No package contains a PE or Mach-O file or a jar, whl, zip or nupkg archive, no file or archive member is named like libc, the dynamic loader, libpthread, libm, libdl, librt, crt1 or a gconv module, and no ELF file or archive member carries the glibc version banner. glibc is shipped in glibc's own packages, such as libc6.

Checked the contents of every published binary package of postgresql-17 17.11 and 17.12, in all of their published revisions (postgresql-17, postgresql-client-17, libpq5, libpq-dev, libecpg6, libecpg-dev, libecpg-compat3, libpgtypes3, postgresql-plperl-17, postgresql-plpython3-17, postgresql-pltcl-17, postgresql-server-dev-17 and the matching debug-symbol packages) for amd64 and arm64 in the DHI Debian repository: none of them contains a copy of libc.so.6, the dynamic loader or libc.a. Every ELF file in them (the server, the client programs, the shared libraries and the server extension modules) is a dynamically linked executable or shared object that uses the system C library at run time, the static libraries they ship (libpq.a, libecpg.a, libpgtypes.a, libpgport.a, libpgcommon.a and their peers) hold only PostgreSQL's own object files, and the debug-symbol packages hold only detached debug information. glibc reaches an image only through the separate libc6 package, which is not part of this owner.

CVE-2019-1010023 is in the dynamic loader of the GNU C Library (glibc), which ldd uses and which can be made to map a crafted ELF file over itself, https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=22851: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2019-1010023. This package does not contain glibc. Checked the contents of every published python3-pip and python3-pip-whl package, from 26.1.2 to the current 26.3, in the DHI Debian repository: apart from Python source, package metadata and data files, they hold the pip .whl file and the Windows launcher executables (t32.exe, t64.exe, t64-arm.exe, w32.exe, w64.exe and w64-arm.exe) that pip's bundled distlib carries, with no ELF binaries in them or inside the wheel, and none of them contains a copy of libc.so.6, the dynamic loader or libc.a. glibc reaches an image only through the separate libc6 package, which is not part of this owner.
